publication.title: Neron Models
publication.authors: S. Bosch, W. Luetkebohmert and M. Raynaud
publication.locator: Definition1.2/1 printed12; Proposition1.2/8 and proof printed15.
publication.corrections: Only the stated mapping property and abelian-scheme case are used.

available_assertion.statement: An abelian scheme over a Dedekind base is the Neron model of its generic fibre; every generic map from a smooth base scheme extends uniquely to it.
available_assertion.objects: Dedekind base, abelian scheme target, smooth source scheme.
available_assertion.hypotheses: The target is an abelian scheme and the source is smooth over the same Dedekind base.
available_assertion.quantifiers: Every generic-fibre morphism from such a source.
available_assertion.parameter_range: No requirement that the source be a group scheme.
available_assertion.uniformity: The extension is unique for the fixed morphism.
available_assertion.normalizations: The Neron mapping property extends morphisms, not merely rational points.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: No arbitrary singular source or bad-reduction abelian scheme is asserted.
available_assertion.limit_order: Verify target is abelian and source is smooth, then extend the generic map.

needed: The actual L-defined isogeny mu_sigma from sigma A to A extends uniquely over their good local abelian schemes at v.
derivation: At the chosen v the two actual generic fibres have good abelian models over O_(L_v); the source model is smooth and the target is an abelian scheme over this DVR. Apply the general BLR mapping property to mu_sigma. The extension respects addition and zero: compare the two candidate maps from the smooth product source, and use uniqueness because they agree on the generic fibre. No prime dividing the degree of mu_sigma need be excluded to extend the morphism. The prior good models and actual mu_sigma, rather than any Heegner modular-curve model, are used.
incoming: p outsideT and the actual good models of A and sigma A.
The actual L-defined mu_sigma already constructed; L_v/Q_p is unramified.
boundary: This assertion extends the map; it does not supply good reduction, full-B linearity, or a new finite exceptional set.

available_assertion.statement: Prime-to-residue-characteristic torsion of a good abelian scheme specializes bijectively over the strict henselian base, compatibly with transition maps and homomorphisms.
available_assertion.objects: The good abelian scheme, its torsion and rational Tate module.
available_assertion.hypotheses: Good abelian model, invertible torsion order, finite etale torsion and henselian splitting.
available_assertion.quantifiers: For every instance satisfying the stated hypotheses.
available_assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic-zero number fields and good finite places; the coefficient prime differs from the residue characteristic.
available_assertion.uniformity: Qualitative finite exclusions only; no bound or replacement of either controlled field or exceptional set.
available_assertion.constants: No numerical conductor, degree or height estimate is asserted.
available_assertion.normalizations: Specialization uses the actual Tate module, not a substituted representation.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: No good reduction at the coefficient prime is inferred; bad or ramified places are excluded.
available_assertion.limit_order: Establish finite etaleness and henselian splitting before passing to the inverse limit.

needed: Specialization of the actual prime-to-p Tate modules commutes with the extended mu_sigma and the selected arithmetic Frobenius, giving the action of its reduction composed with relative p-Frobenius.
derivation: For each n, ell^n-torsion of each good abelian model is finite etale because ell!=p. Over the strict henselian base, reduction gives a bijection of geometric torsion points, functorial in maps and compatible with multiplication transition maps. It is equivariant for the residue Galois action. Pass to the inverse limit and tensorQ_ell. The chosen sigma reduces to x→x^p; because L_v/Q_p is unramified, its twist of the source reduction is the p-twist, and relative p-Frobenius maps Abar_v to that twist. Functoriality identifies the composition with the reduction of mu_sigma. Thus u_p is an actual endomorphism of Abar_v and its action on the specialized Tate module is the composed action used in the manuscript.
incoming: Actual unramified L_v/Q_p and arithmetic Frobenius lift sigma.
Good abelian models and the separately extended actual mu_sigma.
The retained finite-etale torsion and henselian reduction-equivalence inputs.
boundary: Coefficient-prime independence of the trace of u_p, its scalar normalization and the two-copy decomposition are separate inputs; this row does not derive the whole compatibility theorem.
